headline: Russian diesel, three weeks after sanctions
summary: Trump said Friday that Putin agreed to release 300,000 tons of diesel at once, 500,000 in November and a million after that. The Treasury issued a licence within hours. Three weeks ago Trump signed a law tightening sanctions on Russian energy. Diesel is $6.28 a gallon, double since the Iran war began. Zelensky called it a gift to Putin.
cover_answer: Yes. The president says cheaper fuel comes first.
table_question: Would you buy from someone you'd punished if it saved you money?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The president made a deal with Russia today to get diesel, the fuel that runs big trucks and tractors. Diesel costs about double what it did when the year started, so the trucks that bring food to the store cost more to fill. Russia attacked its neighbour Ukraine, so a lot of grown-ups are angry about buying from it. That argument is theirs to have, and nothing changes for you tonight.
5-7.why: Trucks and tractors are the fuel. The argument stays with the adults.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script puts diesel in the trucks that bring food to the store and the tractors on a farm, then says why it costs more. One fact about Russia, no sanctions, no Putin. Expect "is Russia bad?" It attacked Ukraine, and the president is buying from it anyway. Say both.

8-12.script: Diesel hit a record $6.52 in September, double since the Iran war began. Farmers and truckers run on it, and voters pick a Congress on November 3. So Trump called Putin: 300,000 tons now, more later, three weeks after a law to squeeze Russia's fuel money. A thermostat turned the other way.
8-12.why: The chain in order, then the dial.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect and whether adults keep their own rules, so the script runs the chain in order: price, farmers, vote, call. The thermostat is the mechanism: the hand that turned the pressure up turned it down. Expect "isn't that cheating?" It is legal; the Treasury wrote a licence. Fair is the open question.

13-17.script: Who pays for cheaper fuel? Three weeks ago Trump signed a law to choke Russia's energy money. Friday he agreed to take its diesel, 25 days before an election. Zelensky says Russia repays "with terror and perfidy." Second: if a price drops because a war runs longer, is that a saving?
13-17.why: A pump price and a far-off war, held at once.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: a price at the pump their family pays, and a war the money prolongs. The script hands them both and asks which counts as cost. Kuhn calls argument a practised skill, so let them argue the other side. Expect "would you take the cheaper fuel?" Answer honestly, then say what would change your mind.

5-7.a: Yes. Russia attacked Ukraine. The president says cheaper fuel comes first.

8-12.a: The Iran war shook oil. Diesel hit a record $6.52 in September.

8-12.q: Does this break the sanctions law?
8-12.a: The Treasury issued a licence letting it out. A House Democrat calls it lifting sanctions.

13-17.a: The White House hasn't said. Zelensky says Ukraine does.

13-17.q: Will it help before the election?
13-17.a: The BBC doubts it: half a day of US use. Early voting has started.
